title: Quantization AMA: prep notes and talking points
content:
Purpose: short technical AMA slot in the March micro-townhall. Audience is company-wide but mostly engineers and solutions folks. Goal: demystify current quantization approach, set expectations for upcoming rolling deployments, and capture feedback/questions we should address in docs or tooling.

Format / logistics:
- 5 minute kickoff (me + Ari): TL;DR and concrete impact on hosted / dedicated / private customers.
- 15–20 minute live AMA: pre-seeded Qs then open mic.
- Live demo optional (5 mins) if infra stable. Backup: video clip of perf charts.

Opening script (concise):
- Hi — quick context: quantization work reduces GPU memory & cost and enables smaller instances for a lot of our open-model catalog. Not magic: tradeoffs exist and we want to be conservative in production.
- What we shipped in canary last week: FP16->INT8 path with revised KV cache layout and fallback to FP16 on quality regressions. Ablation summary: ~2.1x memory reduction on medium-context runs, ~1.25x median latency improvement on small-batch tails.
- Why it matters: lower cost for customers, more capacity per GPU, and better fit for Dedicated burst modes.
- Ask from the company: help us prioritize the workloads we test (examples below) and flag any customer stories that show subtle failure modes.

Pre-seeded Qs + suggested responses:
1) Q: Does quantization change model outputs / hallucination rate?
   A: Short answer: sometimes. We see small deltas on probability calibration for a subset of prompts — typically low-confidence generation or long-context summarization. Canary checks include rouge/EM on our core eval sets and prompt-level divergence thresholds. If regression > threshold we auto-fallback to FP16 for that model/route.
2) Q: How do we detect quality regressions automatically?
   A: Multi-signal approach: eval-set drift, metric regressions on held prompt-sets, user-side signal (rate of high-confidence 'redo' or rerank changes), and sampling-level statistical checks. We treat these signals as noisy and use ensemble rules to avoid flip-flopping.
3) Q: Private deployments — will customers need to rebuild or recompile?
   A: For most private deployments we provide pre-built runtime artifacts for common platforms. Edge cases (custom kernels, air-gapped infra) may require a minor rebuild; Solutions Eng will coordinate with those customers.
4) Q: Can customers opt out per-route?
   A: Yes. Rollout config will expose a route-level quantization toggle and an automatic health-check window.
5) Q: Safety implications? Are safety models affected?
   A: Safety-critical models are on a conservative default (no quantization) until they pass extra gating (human review + expanded eval).

Potential tough questions to prep for:
- "Why not roll out faster?" => emphasize balancing unit-cost wins vs risk of subtle quality regressions and the cost of rollbacks. Mention observed regression rate and how our gating reduces false positives.
- "How do we prove parity?" => call out evaluation batteries (prompt sets, rouge/bertscore/perplexity, playback tests) and upcoming benchmark dashboard.
- "Will this break customers using custom kernels?" => acknowledge edge cases; provide direct contact path to Solutions / Platform Eng.

Live demo plan (optional):
- Show dashboard: perf delta by route, memory saved by model, canary pass/fail for last 48 hours. If dashboard returns errors, fall back to slides: commit hash + perf table + example failing prompt.

Notes / open items (TODOs):
- TODO: Ari to confirm exact numbers for memory/latency improvements (link PR) before final slide.
- TODO: Ben to draft short doc for Solutions Eng with private-deploy build steps.
- TODO: Create a small 'how to opt out' section in the Console UI docs (product task).
- Open: decide whether to promote INT4 experiments in same announcement or keep separate (recommend separate — too many nuances).

Signals to capture during AMA / follow-ups:
- Requests for per-customer opt-out or rollback history.
- Examples of downstream semantic drift (e.g., tokenizer/embedding mismatch) — capture prompt and route for postmortem.
- Any ask for SDK-level flags (client-side) vs server-side controls.

Slack / followups:
- Post AMA summary to #eng-announce + #solutions with links to artifacts and the opt-out runbook.
- Point people to the QC tracking board (JIRA-ENG-9821) for regressions.

Fallback language for comms if we need to pause rollout mid-week:
- Short message: "We’ve paused the current quantization rollout after observing higher-than-expected divergence on a small subset of prompts. Canary has been reverted for affected routes; we’re investigating and will share findings in 24–48 hours."

Appendix: Helpful links and references (seeded for live share)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quant-kernels/pull/412
- Canary dashboard (internal): CONFLUENCE-QL/quantization-guides-2026
- Tracking ticket: JIRA-ENG-9821

Rough timeline for follow-ups:
- 2 days after AMA: publish FAQ + opt-out docs.
- 1 week: writeup on observed regressions and mitigation strategies (postmortem style).

Meta notes (scratchy):
- Keep language non-technical near top of talk for non-engr audience, but have clear deep-dive answers ready.
- Avoid promising dates for wide rollout — say "gradual, data-driven".
- Capture names of people who volunteer to help expand eval sets (announce next-day doc).

End-of-doc.
